defects.quote: server -- HTTP + SSE, wire schemas --> app
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "a Python backend (HTTP and WebSocket)"; turn 2: "It needs live progress of download and validation runs over WebSocket." The architecture streams runs over SSE instead. AD-07 is titled "pushed by the server over SSE" and lists "WebSocket from the run process to the server" only as a rejected alternative. AD-09 says "Live runs use SSE", the stack table lists sse-starlette, server.stream_run is "text/event-stream", and app PL-42 uses `EventSource`. The developer approved the architecture but never named SSE themselves, so the stated WebSocket choice stands.
defects.fix: Switch the live run stream to WebSocket everywhere. The run process can still write SQLite and the server can still poll by `seq`; only the server→app transport changes. Edits: docs/architecture.md mermaid edge → "server -- HTTP + WebSocket, wire schemas --> app"; PL-01 step 4 → "`server.stream_run` (WebSocket messages of `server.RunEventBody`)"; AD-07 title and Decision → "streams them over a WebSocket"; AD-09 "Live runs use SSE" → "Live runs use a FastAPI WebSocket"; Local API row: drop sse-starlette. docs/packages/server/contract.md server.stream_run → "`WS /api/runs/{id}/events` → JSON messages of RunEventBody". docs/packages/server/pipelines.md PL-34 step 3 "over SSE" → "over the WebSocket", and the sketch return type `EventSourceResponse` → a WebSocket handler. docs/packages/server/architecture.md Overview and the `live` row: SSE → WebSocket. docs/packages/app/architecture.md ("follows one live over SSE", the client row's "an SSE hook") and docs/packages/app/pipelines.md PL-42 step 1 (`EventSource` → `WebSocket`). docs/packages/app/architecture.md Testing: "a mocked `EventSource`" → "a mocked WebSocket".

defects.quote: | M4 | S2 | Covariance ranking | engine, lab | PL-03, PL-14, PL-15, PL-16, PL-17, PL-18 | M1 (data.ReturnsPanel, PL-11 output) | Designed |
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "covariance estimation (sample, shrinkage, denoised) compared on real data". M4 depends only on M1, whose data is the 3-year SyntheticSource (2020-01-02 – 2022-12-30, about 756 sessions). engine.schedule raises "`ValueError` if coverage is shorter than 756 + 21 + 504 sessions", so PL-03 cannot even run on M1's output. PL-03 step 1 and PL-15 also need `data.risk_free`, which the plan defers to M2 ("DATA-06, PANEL-06 (to M2: `FredSource`)"). Real data only arrives in M3.
defects.fix: Set M4's Depends to "M2 (data.risk_free, FredSource), M3 (real Sharadar snapshot, PL-09 output)". Add to M4's Outline/Exit that the ranking runs on a promoted real-data snapshot.

defects.quote: then the skill tests the mean per-period cross-sectional rank correlation with the target against zero
defects.evidence: Turn 1, Stage 3: "build candidate features, then test them with ML for information gain over the residual (market-removed) returns". The spec, lab architecture (`significance` = "Per-feature rank-IC tests") and PL-20 (`rank_ic` → `test_features`) test each feature only by univariate Spearman IC. No model is fitted, so the 'ML' half of the stage is missing. A grep for ML or machine learning in the docs finds only brief Goal 4.
defects.fix: Add a requirement SIG-05 (keep the existing IDs): per walk-forward period, fit an ML model (e.g. a regularised linear model and a gradient-boosted tree on the training window, guard-checked) of the 5-day residual target on the candidate features. Measure each feature's out-of-sample information gain as the drop in per-period rank IC or loss when the feature is permuted or dropped. Test that gain against zero as a registered SIG hypothesis with the `null-hypothesis-testing` skill, corrected across the family. Mirror it in docs/packages/lab/architecture.md (`significance` row), docs/packages/lab/pipelines.md PL-20 (new steps after `rank_ic`, e.g. `ml_gain`), docs/architecture.md (a new AD for the model choice; stack row for scikit-learn/lightgbm) and docs/roadmap.md M6 outline.

defects.quote: `SyntheticSource(seed=7)` satisfies data.Source: 505 members on every XNYS session 2020-01-02 – 2022-12-30, every plants-s1 event present
defects.evidence: docs/packages/data/tests.md says "A case's `extra` plants are layered on the base set for that case only". TC-15 (corrupt bars), TC-16 (planted returns plus an override), TC-17 (duplicate bars), TC-18 (511 members, a gap), TC-19 (a mis-stated split), TC-22 (a kill after 250 stocks) and TC-23 (transient errors, no rows) all need SyntheticSource to apply extras, as do the update run's new sessions 2023-01-03–05. M1-T04's packet and acceptance never mention extras, and no later task lists `vendors_synthetic/source.py` in its Writes. M1-T04 is also sized XS for the generator every golden case depends on (505 stocks, all plants, `truth`, the update run).
defects.fix: Add to M1-T04's acceptance: "applies a case's `extra` plants from its `input.json` (corrupt bars, planted returns, duplicate rows, extra members, a wrong action ratio, failing stocks, a stop after N stocks) and serves the update run's new sessions and revision". Add the data tests.md intro paragraph (the extras rule) to its Read line. Change Size to M.

defects.quote: The minimum-variance portfolio's after-cost results are stored as the benchmark for S4.
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "Both must beat the stage-2 classical portfolios out of sample"; turn 2: "Classical portfolios are compared out of sample on realized variance first. ML-driven ones must beat them." The spec stores and compares against minimum variance only (PORT-05, FPORT-01/02, AGENT-03, VERD), so a forecast portfolio could be declared a winner while losing on Sharpe to risk parity, HRP or equal weight.
defects.fix: Store all four PORT results as S4 benchmarks (PORT-05: "Each classical portfolio's after-cost results are stored…"). Have FPORT-01/02 and AGENT-03 compare against the best classical portfolio on the judged metric (lowest variance, highest Sharpe), or against each of them. Update VERD-02, docs/packages/lab/contract.md `lab.benchmark`, PL-19 `store_benchmark`, PL-25/PL-26 `benchmark` steps, and docs/brief.md Not doing ("can't beat minimum variance").

defects.quote: `def training_window(period: TestPeriod, *, horizon: int, length: int | None = 756, calendar: Calendar) -> Window`
defects.evidence: The first test period starts at session 757 (WFWD-02), and the gap is max(5, horizon). A rolling 756-session window ending `gap` sessions before 757 would have to start before session 1, so the default length can't hold for early periods and the contract doesn't say what happens. TC-60 assumes "The window's 756 sessions hold equal counts of 8 and 12, so its mean is 10" (1e-9 tolerance). TC-68 assumes "any 756-session window (28 whole periods) has correlation exactly I". With gap 5 the window has at most 751 sessions, so the mean is 7508/751 ≈ 9.997 and the Fourier correlation isn't exactly I.
defects.fix: State in engine.Window/training_window (and AD-10) that a rolling window is truncated at coverage start, giving `train_start` = max(coverage start, train_end − length + 1). Then rederive TC-60 (mean over the truncated window) and TC-68 (use a window length that is a multiple of 27, or a tolerance that covers the off-diagonal correlation) in docs/packages/models/tests.md.

defects.quote: so a position held through a mid-period removal stays at its last value until the next rebalance and loses the price move after removal
defects.evidence: A stock dropped from the index mid-period still trades and a real holder keeps earning its return until the next rebalance. Freezing it at its last value misstates realised variance and return for every method that held it. Index deletions are not random, so this biases the backtest. BTEST-01 says weights "drift with each stock's returns until the next rebalance".
defects.fix: Have engine.backtest apply held positions' returns from a panel not masked by membership (e.g. `data.returns_panel(..., members_only=False)` or `bars_panel` closes) until the next rebalance. Update AD-23 Consequences, engine.backtest Invariants and PL-15 step 1, and add a closed-form case to docs/packages/engine/tests.md.

defects.quote: the same bundle gives forecasts within 1e-6 on either
defects.evidence: FCST-07 only promises a match "re-run on the same hardware". CPU and CUDA kernels use different reduction orders, so float32 forecasts from LocalTrainer and GpuTrainer generally differ by more than 1e-6 even with deterministic algorithms on. The invariant promises something that can't be met.
defects.fix: Replace it with "re-running the same bundle on the same device type gives forecasts within 1e-6 (FCST-07); CPU and GPU results are compared only within a looser documented tolerance".

defects.quote: | 14 | `run_baselines` | forecasters.baselines | Bundle, ForecastRun → ForecastRun | trailing 63-day vol, EWMA vol, zero return | FCST-05, FCST-06 |
defects.evidence: FCST-06 also requires "its rank correlation must also exceed the best single surviving S3 feature's". No step computes the best surviving feature's IC or tests against it, and models/tests.md lists FCST-06 as uncovered.
defects.fix: Add to `run_baselines` (or a new step): "the best surviving S3 feature's per-period rank IC, used as an extra FCST-RET comparison". Mention it in `test_forecasts`.
